scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: You type a sentence in Hindi, and a second later it's in Japanese. Is there a giant dictionary doing this?

scenes.name: old
scenes.text: Early translators swapped words and phrases using huge tables, which often gave clumsy, word by word results.

scenes.name: tokens
scenes.text: Today a neural network does it. First your sentence is split into small pieces called tokens, and each becomes a list of numbers.

scenes.name: meaning
scenes.text: The model reads all the tokens together, using attention to see how every word relates to the others.

scenes.name: generate
scenes.text: Then it writes the translation one token at a time, each time picking the most likely next piece.

scenes.name: train
scenes.text: It learned this by studying millions of sentences that were already translated by people.

scenes.name: limits
scenes.text: Idioms, slang and rare languages can still trip it up, so double check anything important.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Split, understand, generate, learn. Follow for more on how things really work.
